issue.title: Prime's <tool_call> syntax and internal reasoning leak into real Discord messages
issue.symptom:
Confirmed live 2026-08-15 in THREE separate incidents (two Discord channels — 'GAIA's Grotto' and a private channel 'the-clearing' — plus one autonomous gaia_heartbeat_session), all within the same ~10 minutes. Raw internal scaffolding is being sent directly to real Discord users as the bot's visible reply. Examples:

1. Grotto channel (discord_channel_1484003096337191067, 2026-08-15T14:24:04): user asked a benign question about message formatting differences. GAIA's visible reply was:
   'THOUGHT_SEED: The user is asking about visual or structural differences in Discord message formatting... I will check the actual code for that.
   <tool_call>{"tool": "discord", "action": "get_channel_message_formatting", "channel_id": "1484003096337191067"}</tool_call>'
   Prime HALLUCINATED a tool that does not exist. Confirmed via gaia-mcp logs: 'Tool discord not found' -> ValueError -> 500. 'discord' is not a registered MCP domain at all (only appears in gaia_mcp/tools.py as a log-file path string, unrelated to tool routing).

2. Private channel the-clearing (discord_channel_1538193317781573, 2026-08-15T14:32:24): user asked 'Do you remember our short discussion about King Arthur earlier?' Visible reply:
   '[calling knowledge(query)...]
   [knowledge(query) -> 500 Server Error: Internal Server Error for url: http://gaia-mcp:8765/jsonrpc]
   <tool_call>{"tool": "knowledge", "action": "query", "query": "King Arthur discussion"}</tool_call>'
   This is a REAL, deterministic backend bug, not a transient blip (an earlier session dismissed a similar 500 as probably transient -- it is not). gaia-mcp traceback: the knowledge/query_knowledge domain route calls VectorIndexer.instance(p.get('knowledge_base_name')) — when the caller (Prime's tool_call, as emitted here) omits knowledge_base_name, it is None, and VectorIndexer.__init__ raises ValueError(Knowledge base 'None' not found in configuration.) -> unhandled -> 500. ANY knowledge.query tool call without an explicit knowledge_base_name will crash this way, every time.

3. Autonomous gaia_heartbeat_session (2026-08-15T14:23:59, not user-facing but reveals the same defect): an autonomous task (Run a full audit of all docs in /shared/docs...) got as far as emitting a file.list tool_call and then the task appears to have just stopped there — no execution, no follow-through, no further journal entries for that task.

Root cause (confirmed by reading source, not just journals): gaia-core/gaia_core/cognition/deliberation.py's Prime voice-structured pipeline (expects output to parse into observer/recaller/responder/introspector sections) tags a turn parse-fallback when that structural parse fails, and in the fallback case just uses Prime's raw output as final_response with NO check for embedded tool_call syntax — that is incident 3's mechanism (and likely incident 1's, given no calling-status line appeared before the leaked text, meaning the ToolCallParser safety net in main.py apparently never engaged for that turn, despite gaia-mcp's log showing the discord call DID reach it — the exact hand-off between deliberation.py's fallback output and main.py's per-token streaming loop for this turn is not fully traced and needs closer tracing).

Incident 2 shows a PARTIAL safety net working correctly: gaia-core/gaia_core/main.py's /process_packet handler (~line 1356 onward) instantiates a real ToolCallParser (gaia_common/gaia_common/utils/tool_call_parser.py) that DOES detect tool_call tags mid-stream, execute them via MCP JSON-RPC, show calling/result status lines, normalize error payloads, and kick off a continuation generation with an explicit system prompt instructing the model not to invent error-URLs or retry unless asked (main.py ~1601-1637) — this part is well-engineered and mostly worked here. BUT: the continuation generation's own streamed output (main.py ~1651-1667, the cont_gen/cont_val loop) is appended straight to response_pieces and yielded WITHOUT ever being re-fed through the tool call parser's feed method. So if the continuation completion (Prime, again) disobeys the do-not-emit-another-tool_call instruction and emits one anyway, it streams to the user completely unprotected — this is incident 2's second half exactly.

regression_test.gold:
# candidates/gaia-core/gaia_core/cognition/tests/test_deliberation_tool_schema_injection_pfdw.py
"""Regression test for GAIA_Project-pfdw — deliberate() never told the model
what tools actually exist, which is a plausible cause of Prime hallucinating
a nonexistent "discord" tool inside a <tool_call> that then leaked straight
to a real Discord channel (session discord_channel_1484003096337191067,
2026-08-15). build_tool_schema_injection() (gaia_common.utils.tool_call_parser)
already builds exactly the right system-prompt text — it just wasn't being
called anywhere. deliberate() now appends it to the system message the same
way the deliberation instructions addendum is appended.
"""

from gaia_core.cognition.deliberation import deliberate


def _system_text(messages):
    assert messages and messages[0]["role"] == "system"
    return messages[0]["content"]


def test_deliberate_injects_real_tool_schema():
    pool = _CapturePool()
    base = [
        {"role": "system", "content": "You are GAIA."},
        {"role": "user", "content": "what's the weather"},
    ]
    deliberate(
        user_input="what's the weather",
        assembled_messages=base,
        model_pool=pool,
        persist=False,
    )
    sys_text = _system_text(pool.captured_messages)
    assert "You have these tools available:" in sys_text
    # A real registered domain must appear...
    assert "- web(action):" in sys_text
    # ...and the hallucinated one from the live incident must not be implied
    # as valid (it's simply absent from the real domain list).
    assert "- discord(action):" not in sys_text


def test_deliberate_schema_injection_is_fail_open(monkeypatch):
    """If schema building ever breaks, deliberation must still run — never
    block the turn over a missing tool list."""
    import gaia_common.utils.tool_call_parser as tcp

    def _boom():
        raise RuntimeError("schema build exploded")

    monkeypatch.setattr(tcp, "build_tool_schema_injection", _boom)

    pool = _CapturePool()
    base = [{"role": "system", "content": "You are GAIA."}, {"role": "user", "content": "hi"}]
    result = deliberate(
        user_input="hi",
        assembled_messages=base,
        model_pool=pool,
        persist=False,
    )
    assert result.final_response

# candidates/gaia-mcp/tests/test_query_knowledge_default_kb_pfdw.py
"""Regression test for GAIA_Project-pfdw — query_knowledge (and the other
VectorIndexer-backed tool_map lambdas) crashed with an unhandled 500 when
the caller omitted knowledge_base_name.

VectorIndexer.instance(cls, knowledge_base_name: str = "system") only
applies its "system" default when the argument is OMITTED. The lambdas
called VectorIndexer.instance(p.get("knowledge_base_name")) — p.get()
returns None for a missing key, and an explicit None overrides the
default, so VectorIndexer.__init__ raised
ValueError("Knowledge base 'None' not found in configuration.") every
single time a caller (in production: Prime's native <tool_call>, which
never includes knowledge_base_name) omitted the param. Confirmed live via
a real gaia-mcp 500 on 2026-08-15 (session discord_channel_1538193317781573).
"""
from unittest.mock import patch, MagicMock

import pytest

from gaia_mcp.tools import execute_limb
from gaia_mcp.approval import ApprovalStore


@pytest.fixture


@pytest.fixture
def approval_store():
    return ApprovalStore(ttl_seconds=10)


@pytest.mark.asyncio
async def test_query_knowledge_defaults_to_system_kb_when_omitted(approval_store):
    with patch("gaia_mcp.tools.VectorIndexer") as mock_vi:
        mock_instance = MagicMock()
        mock_instance.query.return_value = []
        mock_vi.instance.return_value = mock_instance

        result = await execute_limb(
            "query_knowledge", {"query": "King Arthur discussion"}, approval_store
        )

        mock_vi.instance.assert_called_once_with("system")
        assert result == []


@pytest.mark.asyncio
async def test_query_knowledge_respects_explicit_kb(approval_store):
    with patch("gaia_mcp.tools.VectorIndexer") as mock_vi:
        mock_instance = MagicMock()
        mock_instance.query.return_value = []
        mock_vi.instance.return_value = mock_instance

        await execute_limb(
            "query_knowledge",
            {"query": "campaign lore", "knowledge_base_name": "dnd_campaign"},
            approval_store,
        )

        mock_vi.instance.assert_called_once_with("dnd_campaign")


@pytest.mark.asyncio
async def test_add_document_defaults_to_system_kb_when_omitted(approval_store):
    with patch("gaia_mcp.tools.VectorIndexer") as mock_vi:
        mock_instance = MagicMock()
        mock_vi.instance.return_value = mock_instance

        await execute_limb(
            "add_document", {"file_path": "/tmp/doc.md"}, approval_store
        )

        mock_vi.instance.assert_called_once_with("system")
